metaTitle: Help & Emergency in Korea: Numbers & What to Do (2026) — Korea Trip Hub
metaDesc: Emergency numbers for Korea (112 police, 119 fire/ambulance, 1330 tourist hotline, 1345 immigration), what to do if you're sick, lose your passport or need your embassy, plus the official emergency app.
tldr: Three numbers cover almost everything: 112 (police), 119 (fire/ambulance), 1330 (24h tourist hotline).
1330 will interpret for you and can call 112/119 on your behalf — it's the easiest first call.
On a 112/119 call, say 'Hello, English please' to reach interpretation.
Lost passport? File a police report, then contact your embassy. Install the Emergency Ready App.

situations.title: What to do if…
situations.intro: Common travel emergencies and the fastest way through each.

cards.name: You're sick or injured
steps: For an emergency, call 119 (say 'English please') or go to a hospital emergency room.
For minor issues, a pharmacy (약국) or walk-in clinic is quick and cheap.
Bring your passport and a card; keep any receipts for travel-insurance claims.

cards.name: You lose your passport
steps: Report it at the nearest police station (경찰서) or substation (파출소) and get the report document.
Take the report + any ID to your country's embassy for a replacement or emergency travel document.
1330 can help you find the police station and your embassy, and interpret.

cards.name: You lose an item
steps: Retrace and ask staff — lost property is very often handed in.
For taxis/subway, call 1330 for help contacting the operator's lost & found.
For anything stolen, file a police report (112) for insurance.

cards.name: A storm, heatwave or alert
steps: Follow official alerts; the Emergency Ready App shows shelters and guidance.
In a typhoon/heavy rain, avoid rivers and low underpasses; check the KMA forecast.
1330 can advise and interpret if you're unsure what an alert means.

items.name: Emergency Ready App
items.d: Official app: nearest hospitals, police stations, shelters, safety guides and embassy contacts.

items.name: 1330 (call or chat)
items.d: The Korea Tourism hotline — 24/7 multilingual help and 3-way interpretation to emergency services.

items.name: Naver Map / KakaoMap
items.d: Find the nearest hospital, pharmacy or police station fast, with directions.

embassy.title: Reaching your embassy
embassy.body: For a lost passport, arrest, or serious emergency, your own country's embassy or consulate in Korea is the place to turn — they issue emergency travel documents and can advise. Search '[your country] embassy Seoul' for the current address and hotline, or let 1330 help you find it. Many embassies are in central Seoul.

items.d: 112, 119 and 1330 all offer interpretation. Start with 'English please' — or call 1330 first and let them relay.
You usually pay upfront (card is fine) and claim later on travel insurance. Keep receipts and reports.
Emergency calls (112/119) work even without a local SIM or credit. Airport/hotel Wi-Fi covers 1330 apps too.
Keep your passport (or a clear photo/copy) with you — police and hospitals may ask for it.

items.a: 112 for police, 119 for fire or an ambulance, and 1330 for anything travel-related (it's 24/7 and multilingual, and can call 112/119 for you).
112 and 119 have interpretation — say 'Hello, English please'. 1330 offers help in several languages including English, Japanese, Chinese, Russian, Vietnamese, Thai and Malay.

items.q: What if I lose my passport?
items.a: File a police report first, then take it to your embassy for a replacement or emergency travel document. 1330 can help you locate both and interpret.
Yes — the official 'Emergency Ready App' shows nearby hospitals, police stations, shelters, safety guidance and embassy contacts.

items.q: Do emergency calls work without a SIM?
items.a: Yes, 112 and 119 can be dialled even without a local SIM or phone credit.
